definitions.explanation: The small metal tab you lift to open a drink can. Strictly the modern stay-on tab, though Japanese uses the word for the detachable rings of older cans as well.

examples.japanese: プルタブを{引|ひ}いて{開|あ}ける。
examples.english: Pull the tab to open it.

examples.japanese: {爪|つめ}が{割|わ}れそうでプルタブが{開|あ}けられない。
examples.english: I can't get the pull tab open without breaking a nail.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}では{車|くるま}いすを{寄付|きふ}するためにプルタブを{集|あつ}める{活動|かつどう}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: At elementary schools, the drive to collect pull tabs to donate wheelchairs still goes on.

notes:
From English "pull tab." The maker's own term is {缶|かん}{蓋|ぶた} or ステイオンタブ, but ordinary speech uses プルタブ for any drink-can opener tab.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- プルタブを{引|ひ}く / {開|あ}ける: to pull / open the tab
- プルタブを{集|あつ}める: to collect pull tabs (for charity)
- プルタブ{式|しき}の{缶|かん}: a pull-tab can

CULTURAL NOTE:
Collecting プルタブ to trade for wheelchairs is a long-running school and workplace charity activity in Japan, familiar enough that the phrase プルタブ{集|あつ}め needs no explanation — even though recycling the whole can is now generally more effective.
